### PE_MSQ_14: Which neuroglial cells reside within the Central Nervous System (CNS)? (Select all that apply)

- [ ] A) Astrocytes
- [ ] B) Oligodendrocytes
- [ ] C) Microglia
- [ ] D) Ependymal cells
- [ ] E) Schwann cells

> **✅ Answers:** A) Astrocytes, B) Oligodendrocytes, D) Microglia, E) Ependymal cells
> **Explanation:** CNS neuroglia = Astrocytes, Oligodendrocytes, Microglia, Ependymal. Schwann = PNS.

### PE_MSQ_15: Select all characteristics belonging to Red Muscle fibres:

- [ ] A) High myoglobin content
- [ ] B) Rich blood capillary network
- [ ] C) Abundant mitochondria
- [ ] D) Fast-twitch rapid fatigue
- [ ] E) Aerobic respiration

> **✅ Answers:** A) High myoglobin content, B) Rich blood capillary network, C) Abundant mitochondria, E) Aerobic respiration
> **Explanation:** Red muscle is rich in myoglobin/mitochondria, slow-twitch, aerobic, fatigue-resistant.

### PE_MSQ_16: Which anatomical structures contain Bipolar Neurones? (Select all that apply)

- [ ] B) Olfactory epithelium of nasal cavity
- [ ] C) Cerebral cortex
- [ ] D) Dorsal root ganglion
- [ ] E) Cochlea inner ear vestibular organ

> **✅ Answers:** A) Retina of eye, B) Olfactory epithelium of nasal cavity, E) Cochlea inner ear vestibular organ

### PE_MSQ_17: Select all tissue macrophages derived from blood monocytes:

- [ ] A) Kupffer cells (Liver)
- [ ] B) Microglia (Brain)
- [ ] C) Dust cells / Alveolar macrophages (Lungs)
- [ ] D) Langerhans cells (Skin)
- [ ] E) Fibroblasts

> **✅ Answers:** A) Kupffer cells (Liver), B) Microglia (Brain), C) Dust cells / Alveolar macrophages (Lungs), D) Langerhans cells (Skin)
> **Explanation:** Kupffer, Microglia, Dust cells, Langerhans are all specialized monocyte-derived histocytes.

### PE_MSQ_18: Which features distinguish Cardiac Muscle from Skeletal Muscle? (Select all that apply)

- [ ] A) Involuntary autonomic control
- [ ] B) Branched cardiocyte arrangement
- [ ] C) Presence of Intercalated Discs
- [ ] D) Complete resistance to fatigue
- [ ] E) Syncytial multinucleated fibres

> **✅ Answers:** A) Involuntary autonomic control, B) Branched cardiocyte arrangement, C) Presence of Intercalated Discs, D) Complete resistance to fatigue
> **Explanation:** Cardiac muscle is involuntary, branched, has intercalated discs, never fatigues, single nucleus per cell.

### PE_MSQ_19: Select all statements true regarding Bone architecture:

- [ ] A) Matrix contains 65% inorganic calcium salts (Ossein)
- [ ] B) Covered externally by Periosteum
- [ ] C) Osteocytes reside in lacunae connected by canaliculi
- [ ] D) Highly vascular tissue
- [ ] E) Matrix is avascular chondrin

> **✅ Answers:** A) Matrix contains 65% inorganic calcium salts (Ossein), B) Covered externally by Periosteum, C) Osteocytes reside in lacunae connected by canaliculi, D) Highly vascular tissue
> **Explanation:** Bone has 65% inorganic ossein, periosteum sheath, canaliculi, vascular supply.

### PE_MSQ_20: Which factors are required during the blood clotting cascade to form Fibrin? (Select all that apply)

- [ ] A) Calcium ions (Ca2+)
- [ ] B) Thromboplastin
- [ ] C) Prothrombin
- [ ] D) Fibrinogen
- [ ] E) Heparin

> **✅ Answers:** A) Calcium ions (Ca2+), B) Thromboplastin, C) Prothrombin, D) Fibrinogen
> **Explanation:** Clotting requires Thromboplastin, Ca2+, Prothrombin, Thrombin, Fibrinogen. Heparin is an anticoagulant.

- [ ] B) Venules

- [ ] D) Lymphatic vessels

### MSQ_P_H_09: Select all factors contributing to the resting membrane potential of a neurone: (Select all that apply)

- [ ] A) Active Na+/K+ ATPase pump (3 Na+ out, 2 K+ in)
- [ ] B) High permeability of resting membrane to K+
- [ ] C) Low permeability of resting membrane to Na+
- [ ] D) Presence of non-diffusible negative proteins inside cyton
- [ ] E) Influx of calcium ions

> **✅ Answers:** A) Active Na+/K+ ATPase pump (3 Na+ out, 2 K+ in), B) High permeability of resting membrane to K+, C) Low permeability of resting membrane to Na+, D) Presence of non-diffusible negative proteins inside cyton
> **Explanation:** Resting potential (-70mV) is maintained by Na+/K+ pump, K+ leakiness, and intracellular negative proteins.

### MSQ_P_H_10: Select all true statements regarding White Fat vs Brown Fat: (Select all that apply)

- [ ] A) White fat is monolocular; Brown fat is multilocular
- [ ] B) Brown fat produces heat via uncoupling protein-1 (thermogenin)
- [ ] C) Brown fat is rich in cytochrome mitochondria giving brown color
- [ ] D) White fat serves primary role in long-term energy storage
- [ ] E) White fat generates heat in hibernating animals

> **✅ Answers:** A) White fat is monolocular; Brown fat is multilocular, B) Brown fat produces heat via uncoupling protein-1 (thermogenin), C) Brown fat is rich in cytochrome mitochondria giving brown color, D) White fat serves primary role in long-term energy storage
> **Explanation:** Brown fat is multilocular with rich mitochondria/cytochromes for thermogenesis in newborns/hibernators; White fat is monolocular energy storage.


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Select all true statements regarding Whi" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>
